jobs.description_excerpt:
Job Details: 
 
 
 Job Description: 
 The Role and Impact 

Low Yield Analysis (LYA) engineers are responsible for end-of-line failure analysis of the assembly and substrate process and identifying key mechanisms that contribute to ultimate root cause identification. This can relate to specific electrical failures and/or be driven via understanding in-line defect and process health (for Defect Characterization LYA). Engineers will be expected to conduct hands on lab work, define data acquisition strategies, data analysis plans, and recommend corrective actions/fixes to internal customers. The LYA engineer will utilize strong presentation skills to influence individual process engineers as well as platform teams. Analysis will include both electrical fault isolation (FI) and physical failure analysis (FA) collection. The LYA engineer will also interact with a large team of technicians and engineers to provide guidance and mentoring on a wide variety of FI/FA methods and strategies. Other duties may include process and defect characterization and developing innovative techniques/approaches to accelerate failure identification and root cause mechanism understanding. LYA engineers will be expected to provide consultation concerning packaging/assembly challenges and work with partner organizations towards improvements in the manufacturing process. The ability to rapidly respond to customer/client requests or events as they occur while developing solutions utilizing formal education and engineering judgment will be anticipated.

 Responsibilities: 

 Lead end-to-end investigations to identify and resolve complex yield, defect, and quality issues.
 Support equipment installation and start-up of advanced analytical equipment.
 Serve as a technical owner for major factory, platform, or technology development programs.
 Define characterization strategies, learning plans, and root cause methodologies for critical technical challenges.
 Utilize advanced analytical techniques including Optical Microscopy, SEM/EDS, EBSD, CSAM, FTIR, Raman, FIB, ion milling, and mechanical cross-sectioning to identify failure mechanisms.
 Utilize advanced fault isolation techniques including curve tracing, electrical hand proving, EBIC, IBIC, TIVA, LIVA, EOTPR, SQUID, SSM, ELITE
 Correlate characterization results with electrical data, defect inspection data, process history, and manufacturing information to establish root cause.
 Consolidate and analyze large data sets using statistical methods and coding tools to identify yield limiters and emerging trends.
 Develop and implement tools, dashboards, automation, and analytical methodologies that improve learning velocity and analysis efficiency.
 Drive corrective actions and influence process improvements across manufacturing, integration, quality, and technology organizations.
 Lead cross-functional task forces and technical reviews to address high-priority yield and reliability issues.
 Present technical findings, recommendations, and risk assessments to engineering and management teams.
 Mentor engineers and technicians while promoting best-known methods and organizational learning.
 Support future capability development through equipment strategy, methodology development, and characterization roadmap planning.
 Effectively manage multiple high-priority investigations while balancing customer commitments, factory priorities, and business needs.
